content_units: Dinner Playlist Flow

A 90-minute set for a relaxed adult dinner: warm and mellow at the start, a tasteful lift through the middle, then an easy glide into a softer close. The selections stay within your constraints:   18 tracks  ,   clean/non-explicit  , and   under 6 minutes each  .
18-Track Dinner Sequence
1.   Astrud Gilberto — “Agua de Beber” (1965)
- Opens with breezy bossa nova elegance.
- Light rhythm and soft vocals make it ideal for guests settling in and first drinks.
2.   Norah Jones — “Sunrise” (2004)
- Keeps the room intimate and unhurried.
- Its gentle groove bridges classic bossa softness into modern jazz-pop smoothly.
3.   Sade — “Cherish the Day” (1992)
- Adds depth and velvet texture without raising the energy too quickly.
- Smooth, soulful, and sophisticated for early dinner conversation.
4.   Corinne Bailey Rae — “Like a Star” (2006)
- Warm and romantic, but still understated.
- Helps the set feel personal and inviting as the meal gets going.
5.   Bill Withers — “Lovely Day” (1977)
- Familiar, uplifting, and effortlessly easy.
- Introduces a brighter pulse while keeping the mood polished and comfortable.
6.   Basia — “Cruising for Bruising” (1990)
- A stylish jazz-pop lift with subtle sophistication.
- Starts nudging the playlist toward a more rhythmic middle section.
7.   Boz Scaggs — “Lowdown” (1976)
- Brings in soft funk with a silky, grown-up cool.
- This is where the playlist starts to feel more confidently social.
8.   Grover Washington Jr. feat. Bill Withers — “Just the Two of Us” (1981)
- Soulful, smooth, and instantly recognizable.
- Keeps momentum building without crowding conversation.
9.   George Benson — “Give Me the Night” (1980)
- The cleanest point of arrival into upbeat dinner energy.
- Crisp groove and bright feel make it a natural centerpiece.
10.   Steely Dan — “Peg” (1977)
- Smart, polished jazz-pop with just enough snap.
- Peaks the energy tastefully while staying dinner-appropriate.
11.   Michael Franks — “When Sly Calls (Don’t Touch That Phone)” (1977)
- Keeps the groove high but more relaxed after the central peak.
- Witty, suave, and musically rich without overpowering the room.
12.   Incognito — “Still a Friend of Mine” (1993)
- Maintains a buoyant, soulful pulse in the second half.
- Feels modern enough to refresh the palette while preserving elegance.
13.   Simply Red — “Holding Back the Years” (1985)
- Begins the descent with emotional warmth and restraint.
- Slows the energy naturally after the funk-jazz crest.
14.   Sade — “Smooth Operator” (1984)
- Sophisticated and iconic, with a measured late-evening glide.
- Keeps attention gently engaged while easing the room down.
15.   Everything But The Girl — “Missing” (Todd Terry radio-friendly original album mood, 1994)
- Adds reflective, atmospheric pop-soul texture.
- Good for the point in dinner when conversation turns more settled and lingering.
16.   Diana Krall — “The Look of Love” (2001)
- A lush, candlelit slowdown.
- Brings classic lounge intimacy into the final stretch.
17.   Sergio Mendes & Brasil ’66 — “So Many Stars” (1968)
- Reintroduces a whisper of bossa/jazz softness near the end.
- Elegant and lightly cinematic, perfect for dessert or coffee.
18.   Al Jarreau — “We’re in This Love Together” (1981)
- Ends on warmth, ease, and quiet optimism.
- A gentle close that feels complete without dropping the mood too abruptly.
Pacing Notes by Course
-   Tracks 1–4:   Arrival and first pours — mellow, airy, conversational.
-   Tracks 5–10:   Main-course lift — more groove, more familiarity, still refined.
-   Tracks 11–14:   Comfortable plateau to soft descent — soulful and polished.
-   Tracks 15–18:   Dessert and after-dinner wind-down — intimate, warm, and unforced.
